drhp.business: The Company manufactures and markets phosphatic fertilizers - principally Single Super Phosphate in powdered, granulated and fortified grades - along with complex Urea-SSP, micronutrients and traded/imported fertilizer products, sold to farmers across major Indian agricultural states. It operates an integrated chemical division (sulphuric acid, LABSA) that backward-integrates a key fertilizer input, and a soya seed-crushing business at Indore. Manufacturing units are deliberately located in Western India, where roughly 60% of all-India phosphatic fertilizer consumption occurs.

risks.note: The MD&A describes a challenging global environment of elevated prices for sulphuric acid, phosphoric acid and rock phosphate; sulphur rose from Rs 26,645/MT in April 2025 to Rs 53,687/MT in March 2026 and further to Rs 87,900/MT in May 2026, the highest since the 2008 commodity supercycle, and the Board's Report notes the year was delivered 'despite volatile raw material prices'. SSP economics depend directly on rock phosphate and sulphuric acid input costs.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility, above all sulphur

risks.note: Realisations are set by the Nutrient-Based Subsidy regime and the SSP freight subsidy; the MD&A lists subsidy disbursement timelines as a near-term industry challenge and the SWOT names 'Dependence on government policies' as a weakness and 'Regulatory / subsidy policy changes' as a threat. Any change in NBS rates or delay in receipts hits both margin and cash.
risks.risk: Dependence on government subsidy policy and disbursement timing

risks.note: The Company flags escalating Middle East conflict, the vulnerability of the Strait of Hormuz (through which roughly a quarter of world crude plus substantial fertilizer and industrial raw material volumes transit), constraints on Israeli phosphate producers and Chinese export restrictions as sources of tightened availability and higher input costs; the SWOT lists 'West Asia supply shocks (sulphur)' as a threat.
risks.risk: Geopolitical supply-chain disruption in West Asia

risks.note: Listed as a weakness in the MD&A SWOT - a structural feature of a subsidy-linked fertilizer business where receivables from the Government and seasonal inventory build tie up cash.

Named as a weakness in the MD&A SWOT: selling prices are anchored by subsidy and farmer affordability while input costs move with global commodity cycles, so the spread is not fully within management's control.
'Monsoon variability impacting demand' is listed as a threat in the SWOT; fertilizer offtake tracks sowing, rainfall distribution and reservoir levels, so a weak season directly compresses volumes.

All manufacturing units are in the Western India belt (Indore, Udaipur, Nimbahera, Pune, and Dhule under construction) and the SWOT records 'Limited Eastern India presence' as a weakness - the concentration that makes regional monsoon or state policy events disproportionately important.

Named as a threat in the MD&A SWOT; scale players with lower cost of capital compete in the same subsidy-governed market, and global phosphate rock price volatility is a second listed threat that larger balance sheets absorb more easily.
risks.risk: Competition from larger PSU fertilizer companies

Per the issuer-commissioned ICRA Report (February 2026), the sector is supported by resilient Indian agriculture (healthy reservoir levels, robust crop production sustaining rural demand), a global 'China+1' shift favouring Indian chemical manufacturing, and sustained government fiscal support to agriculture and manufacturing.
